newsitem.title: UK: UK bank lending rises s/a 8.787 bln stg in Q2.
newsitem.headline: UK bank lending rises s/a 8.787 bln stg in Q2.

text.p: Total sterling lending by major British banking groups rose by a seasonally adjusted 8.787 billion stg in the three months to June compared with a revised first quarter figure of 11.249 billion, the British Bankers' Association (BBA) said.
Lending in the second quarter was depressed by the repayment of borrowing associated with the disposal of a subsidiary and by reverse repos falling by some 400 million stg.
Mortgage lending rose by 2.5 billion stg, the second highest figure since the series began and nearly 40 percent up on the second quarter of 1996.

"Strong consumer demand and continuing housing market recovery combined to push the major bank's lending to persons to record levels in the second quarter of the year," BBA director general Tim Sweeney said.

Personal borrowing rose by 4.151 billion stg, well up on the first quarter and the largest increase since the series began in 1991. This included a rise in consumer credit of 1.65 billion stg (3.9 percent), a series record which was 50 percent higher than in the same period a year earlier.
"Whilst there was some recovery in lending to industry and commerce, companies in the financial sector accounted for the bulk of the remaining increase in the banks' lending," Sweeney said.

Borrowing by manufacturing industry was down 40 million stg. Identified lending to the financial sector rose by 1.923 billion stg, an increase of 3.2 percent, though lending by way of reverse repos fell around 400 million.
